entries.note: RENGINE_, DYLD_ and LD_ keys are rejected when the declaration is read, not merely overridden at launch: a project must not be able to re-point the surface reservation, the workspace connection or library injection through the workspace, and a silent override would hide the mistake. The launch still layers the reservation and adapter over declared env as defence in depth. Kept import-free so formats.mjs and games.mjs share it without a cycle.

anchor.snippet: export const rootRelativeDirectory = value => value === '' || rootRelative(value); /* "" is the project root; see sidecar: working-directory */

entries.note: cwd is the one declared path where the empty string is meaningful: it names the project root, which is also the default when the key is absent, so a declaration can state the root explicitly without a special token. Everything else is the same confinement every declared path gets (no absolute path, no drive letter, no backslash, no ".." segment, no NUL), and spawnTerminal re-checks the resolved directory against the root before spawning, so a reader change alone can never widen where a game runs.

anchor.snippet: export const nameOf = record => typeof record?.id === 'string' && record.id ? ` (${record.id})` : ''; /* see sidecar: record-identity */

entries.note: Duplicated from dashboard-rules.mjs on purpose, exactly as rootRelative is: both rule modules stay import-free so the reader and the runtime can share them without an ES-module cycle. It appends the record's own id to the JSON path so a gamesError says which record is wrong ($.games[1] (vtmb-vr).cwd must be root-relative) instead of asking the reader to count array entries; the duplicate-id error keeps the bare path because the index is what identifies the repeating occurrence. The reasoning behind naming records at all is in spec 078: each section fails whole, so the message is the recovery path.
